name: Cross-View Consistent Loss
definition: A loss function that penalizes discrepancies between the residuals of paired views, weighted by their structural similarity, to enforce global coherence and mitigate Gaussian overfitting.
summary: Cross-View Consistent Loss is a regularization term that enforces global geometric coherence by penalizing weighted discrepancies between residuals of adjacent views, distinguishing itself by leveraging structural similarity to mitigate Gaussian overfitting.
